subject: Discovery recap — Reliability & graceful degradation (MedLytics)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena@medlytics.com>, Samir Rao <samir@medlytics.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap — Reliability & graceful degradation (MedLytics)

Hi Lena / Samir —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our call so we all have the same priorities and next steps. Let me know if I missed anything.

Key pain points you raised:
- Frequent service degradations during peak batch runs; last major incident we discussed was ~2026-05-10 (15m spike/outage) where model hosts dropped and traffic failed over slowly.
- No graceful degradation: when the primary model or region is unavailable, current setup either blocks requests or falls back to a much lower-quality model without clear SLAs.
- Lack of regional failover automation across US/EU — manual ops required, which increases MTTR.

Current stack you described:
- Kubernetes-based inference endpoints (self-managed) for core traffic.
- A mix of open models (community) + one licensed model for critical paths.
- In-house routing + a CDN for assets; no unified inference routing/fallback policy.

Success criteria (what would make this a win for MedLytics):
- 99.9% availability on critical inference routes with p50 latency <200ms for short prompts.
- Automated graceful degradation: fallback to compatible model variants or region with bounded quality degradation and clear SLOs.
- Auditability: per-request logs, KV cache traces, and 12-month retention for audit queries.

Proposed next steps:
1) Technical deep dive with Priya to walk your infra and stress scenarios (action: schedule 60-min session).
2) Share SOC2 summary, draft SLA, and a short architecture diagram (attached).
3) Pilot: 30-day Dedicated capacity trial for a single critical route to validate failover/latency.
4) Follow-up: pricing for Dedicated & fallback model licensing; we'll surface options in the pilot plan.

Attachments: SLA-draft-Redwood.pdf (application/pdf), SOC2-summary.pdf (application/pdf), Architecture-Diagram.png (image/png).

Proposed times for the tech deep dive:
- Thu Jul 2: 9:00–10:00am PT
- Thu Jul 2: 3:00–4:00pm PT
- Fri Jul 3: 11:00–12:00pm PT
(Or use my calendar: https://calendly.com/marissa-redwood/tech-deep-dive)

Thanks — happy to refine.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | (415) 555-0134

Subject: Re: Discovery recap — Reliability & graceful degradation (MedLytics)

Hi Marissa —

This looks right — thanks for capturing everything. A couple of clarifications / additions from our side:
- Incident history: the May 10th incident also caused delayed downstream jobs for ~45 minutes due to backpressure, not just the 15m outage window. That’s the main reason leadership wants automated failover and bounded degradation behavior.
- Fallback behavior: we care less about perfect parity in outputs during failover, but we need predictable quality: e.g., degrade to a smaller model with a quantified BLEU/ROUGE-like delta, not a free-form drop.
- Compliance: we will need to ensure audit logs meet our security/compliance checklist (I have a SOC2 questionnaire ready; we can share after NDA if needed).

We are interested in the 30-day Dedicated pilot. Can you include a rough estimate of cost bands and any constraints (e.g., min throughput commitments)? Also please confirm whether regional failover would require DNS changes on our side or if Redwood can handle transparent routing.

I'll check the times and circle back — Thu Jul 2 at 3pm PT should work for me.

Thanks,
Lena Ortiz
VP Engineering, MedLytics
lena@medlytics.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena@medlytics.com>, Samir Rao <samir@medlytics.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Jul 2026 12:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — Reliability & graceful degradation (MedLytics)

Thanks Lena — helpful color. Quick answers to your questions:
- Cost bands: I'll include three sized options for the pilot in the pilot plan (S/M/L) — estimated ballpark will be sent ahead of the deep dive (no commitment).
- Regional failover: Redwood can handle transparent routing and automated failover between regions; no required DNS change on your side for the pilot — we'll use our routing layer and provide a runbook for the production cutover.
- Audit logs: SOC2 summary attached; for more detail we can sign an NDA and provide a longer artifacts package.

Confirming the tech deep dive: Thu Jul 2, 3:00–4:00pm PT. I'll send a calendar invite and include Priya (Solutions Eng) to drive the infra questions. HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/12345/RDW-34921.

Action items (owner):
- Marissa: send pilot plan + cost bands before deep dive (by EOD Jul 2).
- Priya: prepare questions about model fallbacks, quantization, and KV cache behavior (before the deep dive).
- Jonas: prepare a short runbook template for failover scenarios.

Best,
Marissa
